title: SLO resilience scenario lab notebook
content:
Context and purpose:
This notebook captures lightweight experiment plans and metric definitions for a small cross-team spike: quantify how SLOs behave when we intentionally exercise three resilience modes (fallback, degrade-model, regional-evacuation). Goal is practical observability: pick signals that make it quick for oncall and launch owners to detect, triage, and validate automated rollbacks or fallbacks.

Scope and boundaries:
- Surface-level: inference API (generation/chat + embeddings) only
- Layers included: API gateway, router, serving runtime, KV cache, model variant selector
- Not included: billing accounting, long-term storage retention experiments (these will be separate)

High-level experiment matrix (versioned):
1) Cold-cache region failover (simulated): route 30% traffic away from primary region to secondary for 20m while primary is artificially delayed by 400ms add-latency.
   - Objective: verify SLO alert fidelity and rollout fallback behavior (auto-fall back to cached model variant).
   - Key success criteria: alert for increased error-rate <= 3m after start; automatic fallback applied; end-to-end 95th latency for critical route < 1.5x baseline within 5m of fallback.

2) Model-quantization degrade (graceful): switch to a quantized variant for 15% of traffic on a single model family for 30m to test quality regression metrics and operator rollback speed.
   - Objective: observe quality signals (EMB similarity drift, rerank precision proxy) and validate rollback automation triggers.
   - Success criteria: quality-regression alert triggers if eval-prompt set fails > 2x baseline; rollback executed successfully and quality metrics return within 10% of baseline within 10m.

3) API gateway surge + throttling: synthetic client sends spike up to 5x normal RPS for 12m to validate rate-limit alerts and tenant-fairness dashboards (ensure no noisy tenant dominates).
   - Objective: ensure throttling SLI is observable and traffic shaping is reflected in tenant-level dashboards.
   - Success criteria: per-tenant throttle-rate panels populate; operator noise budget reduces by expected amount; no silent client failures beyond SLA window.

Metric definitions (compact):
- request.count: total requests received by frontend (per-route, per-tenant).
- response.latency.p50/p90/p95/p99: end-to-end latency measured at API gateway (include downstream call breakdown tags: routing, serving-runtime, model-inference).
- kvcache.hit_rate: fraction of requests that hit prefix/KV cache (per-model-family).
- model.fanout.count: number of model replicas fanouted to for a request (useful for routing regressions).
- fallback.trigger.count: number of times the fallback policy routed requests to fallback model/region.
- downstream.errors: categorized by error class (5xx-serving, 4xx-client, timeout, rate-limit).
- synthetic.eval.quality.delta: periodic scoring of a fixed prompt set (normalized).
- tenant.throttle.rate: percent of requests throttled per tenant.

Tracing anchors and span design notes:
- Root span: http.request (tags: route, tenant_id, request_id, primary_region).
- Router span: router.route_decision (tags: chosen_model, chosen_region, fallback_reason if any).
- Runtime span: runtime.inference (tags: model_variant, seq_length, kvcache_hit boolean, gpu_id).
- Model span: model.generate (timing broken into forward.pass and kv_lookup if applicable).
- Synthetic eval spans: eval.run (attach score metadata and prompt_id).

Span-level guidance:
- Attach a small, fixed-size string field eval_prompt_id for any request that matches our periodic eval set; helps linking to quality metrics without high-cardinality.
- Avoid free-form "user_prompt" in spans; instead hash or redact to preserve PII and reduce cardinality.
- Include a boolean span tag 'fallback_applied' on router span. That will make it trivial to find fallback chains in trace search.

Dashboard skeleton and operator quickcards (what to show first):
Top row (incident starter):
- Global request rate (top-left) with per-region breakdown and percent of traffic in fallback mode (stacked).
- 95th latency by route (color-coded), with a small marker for current SLO threshold.
- Error-rate (5xx-serving + timeouts) with earliest offending region highlighted.

Drilldown row (triage):
- KV cache heatmap (model-family x region) showing hit_rate and trend arrows.
- Trace-search widget: recent traces where fallback_applied=true + durations.
- Tenant fairness: top-10 tenants by throttle rate and request share.

Quality monitoring row (for model-degrade experiments):
- synthetic.eval.quality.delta over time, shaded by canary vs baseline traffic.
- embedding-similarity distribution for eval prompts (boxplots).
- auto-rollback activity log panel (times when rollback triggered and by what rule).

Alerting proposals (short list):
- SLO-breach-warning: if rolling 10m p95 > SLO by 15% and kvcache.hit_rate < baseline by 20% -> severity P2 notification to oncall and product-owner channel.
- Fallback-flood: if fallback.trigger.count spikes > 50/min for 3 consecutive minutes -> trigger throttled alert and paging for infra-oncall.
- Quality-regression: synthetic.eval.quality.delta degrades by > 10% on canary traffic -> page ML-owner and start automatic rollback evaluation.

Experiment instrumentation checklist (pre-run):
- Ensure eval set loader is active and eval_prompt_id tagging applied for 1h before experiment.
- Deploy trace sampling config to capture 100% of traces with fallback_applied=true for the experiment window; default sampling remains low otherwise.
- Hook dashboard panels to the experiment tag (experiment_id) so we can compare canary vs baseline slices.
- Spike generator config: record exact seed and client headers to replay later.

Data collection and postmortem plan:
- During run: capture an artifacts bundle (dashboards snapshot, sample traces, metric exports for request.count, p95, kvcache.hit_rate, fallback.trigger.count) and store under /observability-experiments/exp-<id>.
- Post-run: short retro template (what tripped early, what was noisy, corrections to metric semantics, update docs).

Open questions and risks (to resolve before next run):
- Are we comfortable using a single eval set across multiple model families (risk: signal dilution)? Proposal: tag eval prompts by model-family and surface separate lines on quality panels.
- Trace storage cost when sampling 100% of fallback traces — need quota plan and TTL.
- How to represent probabilistic fallbacks (when fallback policy flips for a percentage of traffic) in dashboards without exploding cardinality.

Next actions (owners):
- Miguel: wire up eval_prompt_id tagging in router by 2025-10-01.
- Jian: implement fallback_applied boolean tag and set trace sampling override for experiment windows by 2025-10-10.
- Sophie: draft the dashboard wireframe and create initial panels in sandbox Grafana by 2025-10-15.
- Asha (owner): schedule dry-run with SRE and ML oncall by 2025-10-20 and confirm rollback automation hooks.

Notes to self:
- Keep panel queries simple and pre-aggregated where possible; heavy ad-hoc analytics belong in the experiment artifact exports, not the incident dashboard.
- Aim for a single "starter" triage row for oncall with 3 widgets; everything else is supportive.

Appendix: example PromQL snippets (drafts)
- p95 latency by route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) by (le, route))
- kvcache hit rate: sum(rate(kvcache_hit_total[5m])) by (model_family) / sum(rate(kvcache_request_total[5m])) by (model_family)
- fallback spike detection: increase(fallback_trigger_total[1m]) > 50

End of notebook entry.
